†*122. DR. KUMKUM RAI: Will th e Minister of CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Duncan industries at Kanpur are on the verge of closure; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) if not, what measures are being taken for smooth operation of the 
industries? 
THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI 
SUKHDEV SINGH DHINDSA): (a) to (c) A statement is laid on the Table 
of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (c) Duncans Industries Ltd., Kanpur have served a copy of the 
closure notice to General Secretary, IEL Mazdoor Union, which the company 
has supposedly served to Sachiv, Uttar Pradesh, Shram Vibhag, Lucknow. 
The aforesaid copy of closure notice was received in the Department of 
Fertilizers along with the representation dated 7.12.2001 by IEL Mazdoor 
Union addressed to Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers. 
In order to fix the consumption norms at the realistic level, Government 
has revised the consumption norms of the 13 urea units including Ouncans 
Industries Ltd., Kanpur on an interim basis w.e.f. 1.4.2000. These 
consumption norms are based on the actual levels achieved in 1999-2000, or 
the existing level, whichever is lower. The retention prices have also been 
revised correspondingly, ad interim. This revision has led to reduction in 
retention prices in respect of the urea units and consequently recovery from 
those urea units. Such revision is, however, only an interim arrangement and 
is subject to the decision of the Government on the policy parameters for VII 
and VIII pricing periods which will include consumption norms also.

Failure of computers during rail reservations 
*126. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA: W ill the Minister of RAILWAYS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether no alternative arrangement exists in the Railways to tell the 
position of reservations, in case of computer failure;

inconvenience to passengers in such situations;

tell the position of reservations, in case of computer failure? 
THE MINISTER OF RAILWAYS (SHRI NITISH KUMAR): (a) to (d) It 
is a fact that position of reservation on real-time basis is not available in case 
of failure of Central Computers. However, in the event of computer failure 
on the day of departure of train, the position of reservation, updated upto the

Railways have recently, inducted latest state-of-the-art Alpha computers, in 
order to improve reliability. These computers help quick restart of 
reservation services by way of achievi ng speedy system reboot etc. Failure 
rate of these servers is also very low.

THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R. 
BAALU): (a) to (c) Various organisations namely All India Trade Union 
Congress, All India Port & Dock Wo rkers Federation, India Centre for 
Human Rights & Law, Green Peace and Corp Watch including Centre of 
Indian Trade Unions have written to the Ministry of Environment & Forests, 
drawing the attention of the inflow of steel scrap from the debris of the 
World Trade Centre (WTC), New York in to India. An officer from Ministry

routinely imported into the country for recovery of steel. 
The chemical analysis report of M/s. SGS India (Pvt.) Ltd. has shown that 
the imported steel scrap does not contain hazardous constituents up to 
detectable limits.

Crop Insurance Policy 
929. SHRI BRAHMAKUMAR BHATT: Will the Minister of 
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have announced any new crop insurance policy; 
(b) if so, the salient features thereof; 
(c) the manner in which the farmers are likely to be benefited; and 
(d) by which date the said policy is likely to be implemented? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (d) The Government of 
India have introduced National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS) from 
Rabi 1999-2000. The scheme is voluntary for the States/Union Territories 
and has larger scope of coverage in terms of farmers, crops and risk. The 
salient features of the Scheme are enclosed.  (Sec below) 
The scheme is available for both lo anee and non-loance farmers. A loanee 
former is automatically covered as when  loan is availed for notified crop in 
notified area. Non-Ioanee farmers are required to su bmit insurance proposal, 
to the nearest bank branch/Primary  Agricultural Cooperative Society by 
paying requisite premium. A farmer can get entire risk covered, as there is no 
cap on the sum insured. Cl aims become payable if th ere is shortfall in yield 
as compared to Guaranteed  yield. The claims are re leased to banks and the 
banks in turn credit the amount in th e account of the beneficiary farmers. 
The farmers are not required to prove losses or give loss intimation under 
NAIS as it is required in othpr general insurance schemes. 
Salient Features of National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS) 
The Government have intorduced NAIS from Rabi 1999-2000 season to 
widen the scope and contents of Crop Insurance Scheme: 
—   Scheme is available to all farmers—loanee and non-loance both—
irrespective of their size of holding. 
78 

[8 March, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
—  Compulsory for loancc farmers and optional for non-loancc farmers. 
—  Sum-insured may extend to the value of threshold yield of the area 
insured. 
—  Coverage of all food crops (cereals, millets & pulses), oilseeds and 
annual commercial/horticultural crops in respect of which past yiejd 
data is available for adequate number of years. 
—  Among the annual commercial/horticultural crops, seven crops 
namely cotton, sugarcane, potato, chillies, ginger, onion and turmeric 
are presently covered. 
—  Premium rates are 3.5% for bajra and oilseeds, and 2.5% for other 
Kharif crops; 1.5% for wheat, and 2% for other rabi crops. In case the 
rates worked out on the basis of actuarial data arc less than the 
prescribed premium rate, the lower rate will be applicable. 
—  In case of annual commcrcial/hortic ulrural crops, acturaial rates are 
charged. 
—  Small and marginal farmers arc pr ovided subsidy of 50% of the 
premium charged from them. The Subsidy will be phased out over a 
period of 5 years on sunset basis. 
—  To implement NAIS at lower unit of insurance  i.e.  Gram Panchayat. 
 
— It is proposed to set up a separate agency for implementation 
of NAIS.

Statement-II 
Main recommendations of Expenditure Reforms Commission 
1. The ERC has recommended dismantling of the control system in a 
phased manner, leading at the commencement of fourth stage, to a totally 
decontrolled fertilizer industry which can compete with imports albeit with a 
small level of protection and a feed stock cost differential compensation to 
naphtha4.NG based units to ensure self-sufficiency. 
94 

[8 March, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
A. First Phase:  1.2.2001 to 31.3.2002  
In the first phase beginning February 1, 2001, the existing Retention 
Price-cum-Subsidy Scheme (RPS) for Urea units should be replaced by 
group-based Concession Scheme. The existing urea units may be classified 
into five groups with the rate of concession being determined on the basis of 
averaging of retention prices as on 1.4.2000 of the respective group, 
rounding off the averages to the lowe r of Rs. 100 in each group. While 
working out the rates of concession for units, based on naphtha, FOILSHS 
and mixed feed stocks, the Commission has worked out the concession rates 
on the assumption that these units will either import their feed stocks 
requirements or procure these from domestic resources if the latter are 
willing to sell these at import parity price. During first phase itself the 
Commission has recommended that the distribution control mechanism may 
also be done away with. It has also recommended that a special provision of 
Rs. 200 crore may be made to provide freight subsidy for effecting supplies 
in the North East, Jammu & Kashmir and other difficult areas. ERC has 
proposed to deduct Rs. 100 per MT from the concession amounts payable to 
urea units to mobilize Rs. 200 crore for this special freight subsidy. 
B. Second Phase: 1.4.2002 to 31.3.2005  
In the second phase beginning from 1.4.2002, the rates of concession 
payable to the five groups are reduced taking into account the reduction in 
capital related charges in respect of  gas-based groups and the expected 
progress in improving ener gy efficiency in the case of three non>gas based 
groups of units. 
C. Third Phase:  1.4.2005 to 31.3.2006  
In the third phase beginning from 1st April 2005, all the non-gas based 
plants will examine the feasibility of modernisation and switching over to 
LNG. For plants that do not switchover to LNG as feed stock, only the level 
of concession that the unit would have been entitled to would be limited to if 
it had switched over to LNG. However, ERC has also stated that in order to 
achieve the 
95 

RAJYA SABHA [8 March, 2002] 
self-sufficiency in urea production, new plants based on FOILSHS/ LNG may 
also be permitted and provided with feedstock differential cost. 
D. Fourth Phase: From 1.4.2006 
The fourth phase begins on 1.4.2006 when the industry is decontrolled. 
2. 7% Annual increase in MRP  
The Commission recommended a 7% increase in the price of urea in real terms 
every year from 1.4.2001. This way the open market price will reach Rs. 6903 
by 1.4.2006, a" level at which the industry can be freed from all controls and be 
required to compete with imports, with variable levy ensuring availability of such 
imports at the farm gate at Rs. 7000 per tonne of urea. While no concessions will be 
necessary from this date onwards for gas based, FOILSHS and mixed feed stock 
plants, existing naphtha units convert ing to LNG as also new plants and 
substantial additions to the existing plants will be entitled to a feed stock 
differential with that for LNG serving as a ceiling. 
3. Dual Pricing Scheme and Employment Guarantee Scheme 
For protecting the small and marginal farmers against the price rise of urea, the 
Commission has suggested introduction of dual price scheme through tradable 
coupons and expansion of Employment Guarantee Scheme and rural works 
programmes to increase their purchasing power.

Regarding Priorities for Wildlife and Forests 
The details of the wildlife conservation strategy adopted by the 
Indian Board for Wildlife are:—  
1. Wildlife and forests shall be declared priority sector at the national 
level for which funds should be earmarked. 
2. Law enforcement agencies must ensure that those engaged in 
poaching, illicit trade in wildlife a nd wildlife products, destruction 
of their habitat, and such other illegal activities arc given quick and 
deterrent punishment. 
3. We should fully tap the potential in  wildlife tourism and at the same 
time take care that it does not have adverse impact

in wildlife and protected areas. The revenue earned from increased 
tourism should be used entirely to augment available resources for 
conservation. 
4. Protecting interests of the poor and tribals living around protected 
areas should be handled with  sensitivity and with maximum 
participation of the affected people. They should have access to the 
minor forest produce, in the forest outside of national parks and 
sanctuaries. Employment and means generation for these people is 
crucial for maintaining symbiosis between the forests, wildlife and 
the people. People should be encouraged to take up afforestation and 
conservation in new areas. 
5. While strengthening protective measures against traditional threats 
to wildlife, we should also respond to newer threats such as toxic 
chemicals and pesticides. 
6. There should be greater governmental as well as societal recognition 
and support for the many non-governmental organizations engaged 
in wildlife conservation. Mainstream media to better highlight their 
activities as also successes of governme ntal  initiative  that  have  
worked. 
7. Creatively produced Television Programmes on wildlife and 
ecology are widely appreciated by young and old as seen from the 
popularity of dedicated T.V. ch annels like. Discovery, National 
Geographic and Animal Plant. It proposed that Pras ar Bharati and 
other private channels alongwith  with agencies like WWF for 
Nature should collaborate and increase original Indian content in 
different languages on our television. 
8. No diversion of forest land for non-forest purposes for critical and 
ecologically fragile wildlife habitat shall' be allowed.

Destruction of forests by mining in Assam  
 
952. DR.   ARUN   KUMAR   SARMA:   Will   the   Minister   of 
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of destruction of forests and hills on  
account of open cast mining operations in the Patkai Range of Assam by the 
North East Coal Field Ltd. of CIL; 
(b) if so, the details of clause-wise pr otective measures provided in the 
Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulatory) Act, 1957 and those 
taken; 
(c) the extend of damage caused to forests and natural topography, 
vegetation and wild life vegetation, drinking water and cultivable land; and 
(d) the total hectares of land utilised for open cast mining operations since 
inception and the land subsequently reclaimed and made fit for vegetation? 
THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI T. R. 
BAALU): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. De-coaled areas are backfilled with 
overburden, terraced and compacted. Top soil over is spread to make the area 
fit for vegetation. Retaining walls and toe-walls are constructed for protection 
against slope failure. Gullies are plugged. Mine water discharge is treated 
before its final disposal. Mining machinery is properly maintained. Water is 
sprayed on haul roads to minim ise fugititve dust emissions.  
Munchi abandoned mine measuring 35 ha. has been reclaimed and converted 
into a recreation ground with a lake. Pisiculture has been promoted. Plantation 
of ornamental plant species has been carried out. 
(c) Natural topography and vegetation has been damaged due to 
111 

RAJYA SABHA [8 March, 2002] 
mining activities. 55 hectares of cu ltivable land was degraded and duly 
compensated by the project authorities. Compensatory afforestation is being 
carried out in mine degraded areas and other areas as well. No instances of 
disturbance to wildlife and contamination of drinking water have been 
reported. The project authorities have already initiated steps to prevent 
further degradaton. 
(d) Out of 1272.34 hectares of lease hold area, 187 hecatres have been 
disturbed. 84 hectares have been fully reclaimed. The reclamation process 
will continue for five years beyond cessation of mining operations. The 
protective measures adopted by the proponent are being regularly monitored 
by Pollution Control Board, Assam.

Effect  of forest  fires 
955. SHRI RAMACHANDRA KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of 
ENVIRONMENT AND  FORESTS be pleased to state:  
(a) what arc the deleterious effects of forests fires, on the regeneration 
capacity of natural forests, including the regeneration of Sal (Shorca 
robusta); 
(b) whether any study has been undertaken by the Government or State 
Governments in this regard; if so, the findings thereof; 
114 

[8 March, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
(c) whether it is a fact that forests in our country, predominantly Sal, 
are being gradually thinned out by the recurring forest fires, collection of 
leaves, etc.; and 
(d) whether Government have constituted any Technology Mission on 
preventing and combating forest fires? 
THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI T. R. 
BAALU): (a) and (b) Frequent and heav y forest fires cause serious damage 
to the regenerating seedlings of the forest species including Sal (Shorea 
robusta). It also adversely affects th e soil moisture regime and nutrient 
balance. This results in change in vege tation profile of the forest type. This 
has been corroborated by the studies conducted by the Indian Council of 
Forestry Research and Education, Dehradun and other such institutes and 
universities conducting research on forest ecology. 
(c) No, Sir. However, due to biotic pressure, forest fires 
are quite common in forest areas near villages. This results in 
degradation of forests which include the Sal forests. 
(d) No, Sir. However, a National Master Plan for 
prevention and control of forest fires has been prepared by 
the Ministry of Environment and Forest. Based on it funds 
are being allocated to the State Governments under the 
Centrally Sponsored Scheme 'Forest Fire Control and 
Management' for combating forest fires. A national guidelines 
has also been issued to the State Governments for prevention 
and control of forest fires.

SHIKSHA SAHAYOG YOJANA 
Eligibility 
SHIKSHA SAHAYOG YOJANA is available for students studying 
between 9th to 12th standards, whose parents are below poverty line and are

availed if the student fails and is detained in the same standard.

scholarship scheme can be availed for a maximum period of four years only 
and is available for a maximum of two children of the Janashree Bima 
Yojana member. 
Premium

members of the Janashree Bima Yojana. Nodal Agencies are 
128

required to identify the needy students eligible for scholarship from the 
families of Janashree Bima Yojana members and to guide them to fill up the 
application form (available with Nodal Agency). The duly completed form 
will have to be deposited with the Nodal agency. The Nodal Agency certifies 
all the application forms received from  deserving students. The list of the 
beneficiary students is then forwarde d to the concerned LIC P&GS Unit for 
disbursement of scholarship/s. The sc holarship/s will be disbursed to the 
beneficiary students through the concerned Nodal Agency.

beneficiaries will be made from the poorest of the poor students.

Department of LIC of India. Nodal Ag encies are required to maintained 
records and submit certificates/details of utilisation periodically.

1000. PROF. (SHRIMATI) BHARATI RAY: Will the Minister of 
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the crime against women in general and dowry 
related crimes in particular are on the increase; and 
(b) if so, the reaction of Government in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI SUMITRA MAHAJAN) : (a) 
As per the data compiled by the National Crimes Records Bureau, Ministry 
of Home Affairs, a total of 135771 in cidents of crimes against women were 
reported in 1999, 137472 in the year 2000 and 124869 in 2001 (upto 
available months), as per details at statement (Sec below). The total incidents 
of crime against women went up by 1.25% in the year 2000 over 1999 
whereas dowry death cases rose by 3. 92% during the same period. On the 
other hand, cases under Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 decreased by 38.3% in 
the same period. The figures for the year 2001 are incomplete, hence non-
comparable. 
(b) To prohibit giving or taking of dowry. Government has enacted the 
Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, Sections 304B and 498A of the Indian Penal 
Code also deal with 'dowry death' and the offence of cruelty, both mental and 
physical, towards a married woman by her husband or relatives. Section 113-
B of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 pr ovides that Courts may presume the 
guilt of the husband or relative who ha d subjected the woman to cruelty in 
connection with dowry. 
The direct responsibility for implementing these laws is that of State 
Governments and the mechanisms under them. The Government has, 
however, advised all State Governments to appoint Dowry Prohibition 
Officers with independent charge and to notify rules under the provisions of 
the Dowry Prohibition Act. 
The National Commission lor Women is in the process of reviewing the 
Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 to make its provisons more stringent and 
effective. 
Since the menace of dowry is a reflection of women's low status in 
159

society, Government have taken a number of steps to raise the status of 
women and to change societal attitudes towards girls and women. These 
include media campaigns, awareness generation camps, spreading legal 
literacy, counselling, legal aid, support to voluntary agencies and schemes for 
the socio-economic empowerment of women. 
The National Policy for the Empowerrrfeht of Women adopted by the 
Government is also committed to eliminating the incidence of all forms of 
violence against women, including those arising from customs such as 
dowry.

(a) whether an Archaeological site, dating back to 7,500 BC and older 
than hitherto oldest known human civilizations including those found in the 
Valleys of Sumer, Harappa and Egypt, was discovered by a team of Indian 
Marine Archaeologists in the Gulf of Cambay of Gujarat coast;

MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER OF

The National Insitute of Ocean Te chnology (NIOT), Chennai of the 
Department of Ocean Development (DOD), Government of India had during 
the course of under water surveys in  the Gulf of Cambay, Gujarat come 
across a stretch of formations typical of a riverine regime in the middle of the 
sea at 30-40 m water depth. An area of almost 9 km. stretch west of Hazira in 
Gujarat appeared to be lined with well laid house basement like features 
partially covered by sand waves and sand ripples. The Side Scan Sonar 
deployed for the survey picked up images which indicate several geometric 
objects that are normally man made.

Decline in Railway Passenger Traffic 
1030. SHRI    SURESH   PACHOURI:    Will    the    Minister    of 
RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Railway have experienced  a continuous decline in their 
position related to the road transport system; 
(b) if so, the trend during last five years; 
(c) whether the skewed tariff policy in favour of ordinary passenger tariff 
is responsible for this state of affairs; and 
(d) if so, the details of corrective measures taken in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI O. RAJAGOPAL): (a) and (b) The 
latest estimates available for traffic carried by roadways are for the year 
1997-98. As per these estimates and re cords available, the share of Railways 
in the total traffic movement in 1997- 98 shows a decline, on consideration of 
the share in 1950-51 as the basis. The records indicate that for 1950-51 the 
share of Railways vis-a-vis the total traffic movement was 89% for freight 
and 68.4% for passenger. As per Economic Survey of India 1997-98, the 
traffic carried by roadways is 60% of the total freight movement and 80% of 
total passenger movement. Correspondingly, 40% of the total freight 
movement and 20% of total passenger movement in 1997-98 is presumed to 
be on Rail. 
While Railways maintain comprehensive records of the traffic carried by 
them, similar data is not maintained by roadways. As no details for the 
current level of traffic on road is availa ble, the trend of sh are of rail to road 
traffic over the last 5 years can not be estimated. 
(c) A policy of restraint has been followed in the past by the Railways 
towards increasing ordinary passenger fares in keeping with the socio-
economic objectives of the Government. The subsidisation of passenger  
traffic  by  freight   as   also  cross-subsidisation  within 
185 

RAJYA SABHA [8 March, 2002] 
different commodities of freight and different segments of passenger business 
is partially responsible for the declining share of Railways in the total transport 
system. 
(d) Corrective measures with respect to above have been initiated in the 
Railway Budget presented to Parliament for the year 2002-03 e.g. 
(i) Rationalization of freight rate structure to remove the anomalies and 
thereby making the freight rates more attractive. 
(ii) Rationalization of fares for different classes of travel in passenger 
services, with indexing of the fare structure in the upper classes, with 
respect to the second class fare.

Indian Railways, in association with the International Union of Railways 
(UIC) organised a User-Producer interaction programme in New Delhi on the 
subject "Improved Maintenance Practices and Reducing Life Cycle Cost—A 
common challenge for Railway Oper ators and Manufacturers. The 
programme was organised over 3 days from January 30 to February 1, 2002.

new technological developments. The conference was very successful in 
focussing attention on the issues involved.

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF STEEL (SHRI 
BRAJKISHORE TRIPATHY): (a) and (b) As part of restructuring of 
manpower, SAIL proposes to reduce its workforce every year to reach a level of 
1 lakh by the end of financial year 2004-2005. Accordingly, during the financial 
year 2002-2003, SAIL proposes to reduce its manpower by about 16,000 
through introduction of Voluntary Retirement Scheme, natural and other 
separations, and minimal recruitment. 
(c) Yes, Sir. 
(d) and (e) SAIL has incurred loss of Rs. 1290 crore during April-December, 
2001. Aprart from the main reason of fall in steel prices, other reasons for 
incurring losses are as under: 
 High manpower costs 
 Closure of important export markets for the Indian Steel due to protectionist 
measures such as anti-dumping duties, etc., initiated by a number of 
importing countries. 
 Stagnation in steel consumption due to slow down in Indian economy 
leading to oversupply siutation and recessionary trends in the global 
steel market resulting in cheap imports.

Boosting the Steel Industry 
1057. SHRI BHAGATRAM MANHAR: W ill the Minister of STEEL be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Steel industry is going through a lean period and 
Government plan to provide fiscal incentives, to boost the steel industry; 
(b) how much has been spent on research and development out of the 
Steel Development Fund; and 
(c) what are Government's plans to en sure that the money being spent 
leads to better quality of steel? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF STEEL (SHRI 
BRAJKISHORE TRIPATHY): (a) Yes, Sir. The Government has announced 
certain measures in the Railway Budget 2002-2003 and the Union Budget 
2002-2003 to help the domestic steel industry, which include (a) reduction in 
rail freight costs for transporting finished steel, (b) increase in basic customs 
duty on seconds and defectives steel to the bound rate of 40%, (c) reduction 
in Customs Duty by 10% on a number of refractory raw materials to reduce 
production costs in steel industry, (d) exemption of HRSS coils for coin 
blanks from Custom Duty, (e) reduction of Custom Duty on HRGO/HRNGO 
by 10%, (f) public investment in key infrastructure sectors has been increased 
to boost the growth of the core sectors, (g) reduction of Custom Duty on 
Metcoke for COREX units from 15% to 5%. 
(b) A sum of Rs. 58.99 crores has been released from the Steel 
Development Fund (SDF) since 1997-98 for research and development 
activities including improvement of quality of steel. 
(c) Monitoring of the R&D projects is done by the Empowered Committee 
functioning under the chairmanship of Secretary (Steel). However, the quality 
of steel depends upon several factors like the technology and raw materials 
used, operational expertise, innovative programmes and systems available in 
the respective steel plants etc.

REFERENCE ON THE INTERNATIONAL WOMEN' S DAY 
THE DEPUTY CHAIRMAN (DR. (SHRIMATI) NAJMA HEPTULLA) : 
Sir, thank you very much for giving me this opportunity, and I am happy 
that the HRD Minister, Dr. Murli Manoh ar Joshi, is present over here, 
because this concerns his Ministry also,.as this Ministry, apart from other 
things, is responsible for empowerment of women. Sir, this is a very 
important day for half the population of  the world totaling about 3 billion, 
I mean, the women. I take this opportunity to wish you all, the men also, a 
• very happy Women's Day.  
From the same place some six year ago I had moved a Resolution 
that was .adopted unanimously^foz jthe empowerment of women. It led- to the 
formation of the- Parliamentary Committee on Women's Empowerment. I had 
the privilege to be its first Chairperson.. This Resolution gave a greater resolve 
to. all the political parties to allocate mo re tickets to women in elections at all 
levels. And, in the Congress Party, they took a conscious decision to have 33 
per cent reservation at the party level at every stage. From then onwards our 
fight for greater share in Parliament becam e  stronger.      However,   every  
successive  Government   has  been 
243 

RAJYA SABHA [8 MARCH, 2002] 
promising for, giving 33 per cent seats to women in Parliam ent. But so far it 
remains only a dream. We are thankful to the Government for announcing the 
last year as the Year for Empo wering Women. We expected real 
empowerment, and not a declaration only on papers. We are very proud of 
being the largest representative democracy in the world. People idolise of a 
system and draw inspiration from us . Therefore, when we speak of equal 
representation for women, people across the globe look at our figures. They 
question me -- mostly in all the international parliamentary fora -- how our 
resolve for 33 per cent is still crawling at  8 per cent for the last one decade. A 
true democracy has to be representative, enthusive and partipipative. It cannot 
be representative when 50 per cent of t he population is represented by merely 
6 per cent of the total seats in the Parliament. All our efforts would remain 
ineffective unless we are not able to provide basic social security to our 
women. Women are facing multiple source s of violence. While there is raising 
concern about the domestic violence t hat prevents women from exercising 
their rights, I mentioned here, Sir, that t he Bill that the Government is going to

As a result of the women's movement, and as a result of the efforts of

women? Unfortunately, this Parliament has failed in passing a comprehensive 
legislation for the agricultural labour.

We have got so many assurances on the floor of this House. None of them 
has been fulfilled. Last year, this NDA Government announced a Special Bima 
Programme for the agricultural labour. At that time,, the Finance Minister 
emphasised that they are going to implement this special scheme in 50 districts 
of our country and the benefit will be given to five lakh agricultural labourers. 
Now one year has passed. Sir, what is the result? Did they implement in all the 
villages as announced? We have about 100 million agricultural labourers. The 
target was .5 million. What is the ex perience? Sir, the experience shows that 
this Government did not even enrol 10,000 agricultural labourers under the 
Special Bima scheme. It was a failure. The Government did not apply its mind 
to implement this scheme.   This is the approach.    Is there any social security 
measure for the

programme to assist them through providing essential material. No. There is no 
such a specific scheme. Is there any  specific scheme for marketing the

programmes. I would like to know whether the Government, at any time,

announcements. There is no proper impl ementation. Mere announcements will 
not do. There has to be an effective im plementation. Are you serious on these

raw material for women entrepreneurs in the rural areas. And the Government

being forced to look after their families.   They

have become heads of the families. Millions  of workers are migrating. Is there
